name: Pydantic AI
question: How do I get typed, validated agents with little ceremony?
summary: Pydantic AI, from the team behind Pydantic, defines an agent with a model, typed dependencies and a typed output. Tool arguments and final outputs are validated Pydantic models, and invalid output goes back to the model for a retry. It supports most providers through one API, injects dependencies such as a bank client so agents are easy to test, and integrates with Temporal, DBOS and Prefect for durable runs, with Logfire for tracing.
useCases: Python teams who value type safety
Agents that must return structured data
Model-agnostic apps that may switch providers

items.detail: a Pydantic model the answer must match
Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock and more

Run with injected dependencies; test with fakes
Add durable execution for long runs
pitfalls: Putting business state in globals instead of deps
remember: Type the output, inject the dependencies, validate everything.

steps.title: Type the answer
steps.text: Reply is a Pydantic model with a fixed set of statuses. Downstream code can switch on status without parsing text.

steps.title: Declare dependencies
steps.text: deps_type=Bank says what every run receives. Tools use ctx.deps instead of globals, so tests pass a fake bank.

steps.title: Typed tools
steps.text: Arguments are validated before the tool runs; the schema is generated from the type hints and docstring.

steps.title: Approval through the dependency
steps.text: The approval service is part of the injected bank, so a test can approve or reject automatically.

steps.title: Any provider, one string
steps.text: Switching from Anthropic to OpenAI or Google is a change to the model string, not a rewrite.

steps.title: A validated result
steps.text: result.output is a Reply. If the model returns something invalid, Pydantic AI sends the error back and retries.

practice.scenario: A fictional wealth-tech firm needed its support agent to return a structured status that downstream systems could act on, and wanted freedom to switch model providers. In Pydantic AI the agent returns a validated Reply model, and the bank client is injected as a dependency, so tests swap in a fake bank. Moving from one provider to another was a one-line change of the model string.

library.name: Pydantic AI
library.what: Typed agents, tools and outputs over most model providers, with dependency injection for testing.

practice.note: Tests can pass a fake Bank as deps and a test model, so the agent’s logic is checked without calling a real provider.

samples.code:
from typing import Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic_ai import Agent, RunContext

class Reply(BaseModel):
    status: Literal["succeeded", "dispute_raised", "rejected", "not_found"]
    message: str

agent = Agent(
    "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5",          # or "openai:...", "google-gla:..."
    deps_type=Bank,
    output_type=Reply,
    instructions=SYSTEM,
)

@agent.tool
async def get_transaction(ctx: RunContext[Bank], utr: str) -> dict:
    """Look up a UPI transaction by its 12-digit UTR."""
    return await ctx.deps.transactions.get(utr)

@agent.tool
async def raise_dispute(ctx: RunContext[Bank], utr: str, reason: str) -> str:
    """Raise a dispute for a failed UPI debit. Needs human approval."""
    if not await ctx.deps.approvals.request(utr, reason):
        return "Rejected by reviewer."
    return await ctx.deps.disputes.create(utr, reason)

result = agent.run_sync("My ₹1,200 UPI payment failed but money was debited. UTR 412345678901",
                        deps=bank)
print(result.output.status, result.output.message)

numericDrill.question: An agent’s output fails validation 8% of the time on the first try. Pydantic AI sends the error back, and each retry succeeds 75% of the time. With two retries, what share of runs still fails validation, in percent?
numericDrill.answer: 0.08 × 0.25 × 0.25 = 0.005, or 0.5%. Validation plus retries catches most shape errors; the remaining failures need handling, and valid shape still does not guarantee correct values.

interview.question: What does Pydantic AI add over a plain SDK?
interview.answer: Typed agents: an output type that the answer must validate against, with automatic retries when it does not; typed tool arguments; dependency injection so tools get a bank client or database that tests can replace; one API across providers; and integrations for durable execution, tracing and evals.

interview.question: Why inject dependencies into an agent?
interview.answer: So tools do not reach for globals. Passing a typed dependency such as a bank client makes the agent testable with a fake, keeps credentials out of prompts, and makes it clear what each run can touch.
